Published online:
    9 September 2026

Geographic focus:
    Europe (EU-27, with references to Russia, Ukraine, Middle East)

Temporal focus:
    T1. Historical report [YES] — covers EU energy transition since 2022 invasion, past investment commitments vs. actuals
    T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES] — storage at 67% ahead of winter 2026/27, price spike risk
    T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [YES] — Russian LNG ban from Jan 1 2027, €300bn investment gap, grid/renewables buildout

Synopsis:
    EU auditors warn that Europe's plan to exit Russian energy is faltering at a critical moment. Gas storage sits at just 67% — well below last year's 80% — heading into winter, while Middle East turmoil further squeezes global supply. The EU has cut Russian gas dependency from 45% to 12% of imports, but auditors flag the reduction was driven by mild weather and demand destruction rather than structural policy. Only €54.3bn of the €300bn investment envelope has been committed. An upcoming ban on Russian LNG (Jan 2027) adds near-term supply risk. The Commission acknowledged the findings and pledged follow-up.
